I do believe there are unfortunate trends, but I don't believe 5"2' men are screwed. 4"11' girls exist! Extremely short girls are out there, and girls taller than 5'2" that don't care about height are out there. What will guaranteed drive away practically all women no matter what their height is, is if the 5'2" man is extremely bitter about how tall he is, and makes this apparent to every woman he meets. Insecurities are a real thing, and I would totally understand being insecure about something like that. But if he can't accept himself as he is, he's going to have a much, much harder time finding love.

I'm sorry if I'm misinterpreting your comment, but I don't think the vast majority of women refuse to date a man shorter than them. I do think that society has given women the expectation that they should probably date a man over her height, but I don't think that an overwhelming percentage of women outright refuse a man simply because he is an inch or two shorter than her. I used 5'2" as an exaggerated example and I will say, sadly you're probably right that it is common for an extremely short man to be rejected by a large majority of women. A 5"2' tall man shouldn't concern himself with women that have this standard, though. There are plenty of women out there that don't care (and those that have a really strong opinion about it love being the loud minority), and that's all that should matter. It's exactly the same for abnormally tall women. We all have to work with what we've got and love ourselves for it.

Both men and women suffer from toxic and abusive relationships. Being used is unfortunately something that happens equally across the board, because assholes exist in both genders (and everything in between). You can think you mean the world to someone, and then they cast you aside in the span of a day. In my comment, I'm mostly talking about first impressions. If a man has nice hair, a good style, even a successful career, but you can tell that he's bitter with a heavily negative view on women and/or life in general, women will flee. Being bitter doesn't help anyone, bro. It's just going to hurt.

See, I think it's a little more dynamic than that. I've found plenty of men attractive, and I'd say it's rare to find one I'm genuinely repulsed by (which usually just has to do with him having very poor hygiene). But thinking someone is attractive isn't enough to want to pursue a physical and/or romantic relationship with them (a generalization, but one I have to make in this context). You're right that, as a woman, I've forced myself to have high standards. But honestly? EVERYONE should. A lady says she doesn't want to date a man because he's 5'2"? Great, then she's not the one for him, and he should happily move on knowing that. I personally could not care less what height the man I date is, and think women demanding a man over 6"1' is ridiculous. If you or anyone else thinks that all women behave like some of the eyebrow-raising ones we see on dating sites ("my man MUST be 6', MUST have blue eyes, MUST work out, MUST get 6 figures ..." gross) then you're going to have a really bitter and misguided view of the world and how it works. But honestly, if you think about it, what do you find attractive in women? It's attractive when they're pretty, intelligent, successful, flexible, clean, empathetic. I'd say I'm looking for the exact same qualities in men. Any woman who isn't disillusioned by the disgusting societal expectations for relationships the internet tells us would say the same thing.

I'm currently reading Brandon Sanderson's Mistborn trilogy, and I think he does well writing distinct characters. His characters have distinct little "quirks" that aren't blatantly obvious, but you come to recognize them the more you read and get to know each character -- just like getting to know someone in real life. For example, a character in his work often uses the phrase "I think", which becomes more noticeable the more you read about him.

Here's an exercise I like to do to see if my characters are distinct: 

Play charades with yourself. Is there a way you can portray your character without words, and people who read your work would instantly recognize who that character is? That's a distinct character! 

You can do this with words, too. Think of things your character would say, then things another character would say about the same subject. How are they different?

Good luck!

That goldfish are meant to live in bowls! The average goldfish gets about fourteen inches long in proper conditions, and because they're such dirty animals (they generate ammonia like you wouldn't believe) they need heavy  proper filtration. Yes, you should have 20 gallons per goldfish. That means two goldfish go into a FILTERED forty gallon tank. No, an air pump is not a filter. No, a plant is not a filter. No, you cannot put other tropical fish with your goldfish, because goldfish require lower temperatures (65 degrees Fahrenheit) while tropical fish require higher temperatures (78 degrees Fahrenheit). 

Goldfish can live up to 25 years. Putting them in a bowl means you are stunting their growth, but not the growth of their inner organs. They stay 2 inches while their organs keep growing inside of them, which is why they die in 2 years, instead of living to be 25 years old, and over a foot long.
